study type: Retrospective analysis of routinely collected administrative health data
exposure: Maternal factors (e.g., previous livebirths, occupational status, age, CS history)

Fetal/pregnancy factors (e.g., gestational age, placental weight, stillbirth, PROM, obstructed labour, non-reassuring fetal status, breech presentation, multiple birth, eclampsia/pre-eclampsia, oligohydramnios, placenta previa/abruptio placenta/antepartum hemorrhage, cord prolapse, birthweight)
cohort: The study cohort included all births recorded in 11 maternity centres in the Friuli Venezia Giulia region of Italy between 2005 and 2015.
finding: The study found significant variability in delivery mode rates across hospitals in the Friuli Venezia Giulia region, with some centers demonstrating a probable overuse of Cesarean sections even after adjusting for patient risk factors.
mod_finding: The study identified various clinical and maternal factors significantly associated with spontaneous vaginal delivery, instrumental vaginal delivery, overall cesarean section, and urgent/emergency cesarean section, and revealed significant variability and potential overuse of CS across different maternity centres.
birth_weight: <2,500 g (as a risk factor for UCS)
gest_age: <29 weeks (associated with SVD), >40 weeks (associated with IVD), 33-36 weeks and 41+ weeks (associated with UCS)
